--- title: "[CausalGAM]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Causal GAM for treatment effect estimation. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-cookbook/whittaker/causal.py#L163-L647){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python CausalGAM( outcome, treatment, confounders, *, method="partially_linear", family=None, n_folds=5 ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Estimates the causal effect of a treatment `D` on an outcome `Y`, controlling for a set of confounders `X`, using double/debiased machine learning (DML; Chernozhukov et al. 2018) with GAM nuisance models. Two structural forms are supported: - **Partially linear** (`method="partially_linear"`): `Y = theta * D + f(X) + eps`, giving a single constant average treatment effect (ATE) `theta`. - **Interactive** (`method="interactive"`): `Y = g(D, X) + eps`, allowing the treatment effect to vary smoothly with `X` (conditional average treatment effect, CATE). DML addresses the regularization bias that arises when flexible, penalized nuisance models (here, GAMs for `E[Y | X]` and `E[D | X]`) are plugged directly into a naive treatment-effect estimator: the smoothing bias in the nuisance fits would otherwise leak into the treatment effect estimate. Cross-fitting (fitting nuisance models on one subset of folds and evaluating residuals on the held-out fold) together with a Neyman-orthogonal moment condition makes the resulting ATE estimate root-n consistent and asymptotically normal even though the nuisance GAMs converge at slower nonparametric rates. Use `CausalGAM` for observational-data effect estimation where confounding is plausibly captured by smooth functions of observed covariates, and you want valid inference (standard errors, confidence intervals) on the treatment effect rather than just a point prediction. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [outcome]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the outcome variable. [treatment]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the treatment variable. [confounders]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of confounder variable names. Both the outcome and treatment nuisance GAMs use `s(c)` smooth terms for each confounder `c`. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["partially_linear"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : `"partially_linear"` (default) for constant ATE, or `"interactive"` for heterogeneous treatment effects (enables `.cate()`). [family]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Family | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Response distribution for the outcome nuisance model. Defaults to `Gaussian()`. The treatment nuisance model always uses `Gaussian()` regardless of this setting, since DML residualizes the treatment via its conditional mean. [n_folds]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[5]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of cross-fitting folds for DML (default `5`). Each fold's nuisance models are fit on the other `n_folds - 1` folds and evaluated on the held-out fold to avoid overfitting bias. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} Fitting proceeds in three steps. First, cross-fitted residuals are formed for both outcome and treatment: $$\hat\varepsilon_{Y,i} = Y_i - \hat m_Y(X_i), \qquad \hat\varepsilon_{D,i} = D_i - \hat m_D(X_i)$$ where `\hat m_Y` and `\hat m_D` are GAM estimates of `E[Y \mid X]` and `E[D \mid X]`, each fit on folds excluding observation `i`. Second, the ATE is estimated by the residual-on-residual regression (the partialling-out estimator): $$\hat\theta = \frac{\sum_i \hat\varepsilon_{D,i} \, \hat\varepsilon_{Y,i}} {\sum_i \hat\varepsilon_{D,i}^2}$$ Third, its standard error is derived from the empirical variance of the Neyman-orthogonal score $\psi_i = \hat\varepsilon_{D,i}(\hat\varepsilon_{Y,i} - \hat\theta \hat\varepsilon_{D,i})$: $$\widehat{\mathrm{se}}(\hat\theta) = \sqrt{\frac{\overline{\psi^2}} {\left(\sum_i \hat\varepsilon_{D,i}^2\right)^{2} / n}}$$ When `method="interactive"`, a further GAM is fit on the pseudo-outcome `\hat\varepsilon_{Y,i} / \hat\varepsilon_{D,i}`, weighted by `\hat\varepsilon_{D,i}^2`, to recover the CATE as a smooth function of the confounders. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#79e79305 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np from whittaker.causal import CausalGAM rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 1000 x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n) d = rng.binomial(1, 1 / (1 + np.exp(-(2 * x - 1))), n).astype(float) y = 1.5 * d + np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + rng.normal(scale=0.3, size=n) model = CausalGAM(outcome="y", treatment="d", confounders=["x"], n_folds=5) model.fit({"x": x, "d": d, "y": y}, seed=0) print(model.treatment_effect()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` TreatmentEffect(ate=1.4973, se=0.0095, p=0.0000, 95% CI=[1.4786, 1.5160]) ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
confounders Names of the confounder variables `X` controlled for in the nuisance GAMs.
is_fitted Whether `fit()` has been called successfully on this model.
method Structural form used for estimation.
outcome Name of the outcome variable `Y` used when constructing this model.
treatment Name of the treatment variable `D` used when constructing this model.
### [confounders]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Names of the confounder variables `X` controlled for in the nuisance GAMs. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [confounders]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns a copy, so mutating the returned list does not affect the model. ::: ### [is_fitted]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether `fit()` has been called successfully on this model. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [is_fitted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Most other methods (`treatment_effect()`, `cate()`, `residuals()`, `summary()`) raise `RuntimeError` if this is `False`. ::: ### [method]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Structural form used for estimation. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Either `"partially_linear"` (constant ATE) or `"interactive"` (heterogeneous treatment effects, enabling `.cate()`). ::: ### [outcome]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Name of the outcome variable `Y` used when constructing this model. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [outcome]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [treatment]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Name of the treatment variable `D` used when constructing this model. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [treatment]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
cate() Estimate conditional average treatment effects.
fit() Fit the causal GAM via cross-fitted DML.
residuals() Return the orthogonalized residuals.
summary() Build a human-readable text summary of the fitted causal GAM.
treatment_effect() Compute the average treatment effect with inference.
### [cate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Estimate conditional average treatment effects. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-cookbook/whittaker/causal.py#L489-L573){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python cate(new_data=None, *, variable=None, n_points=100, level=0.95) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Requires `method="interactive"`. Evaluates the fitted CATE model (a GAM regressed on the pseudo-outcome `\hat\varepsilon_Y / \hat\varepsilon_D`) either on user-supplied `new_data` or on a grid over one confounder, holding the other confounders at their training-data means. Returns CATE as a function of a chosen confounder variable, together with pointwise confidence bands derived from the CATE model's own standard errors. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [new_data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [InputData | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Covariate data for prediction. If `None`, evaluates on a grid of the specified variable. [variable]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confounder to condition on. Required if `new_data` is `None`. Defaults to the first confounder. [n_points]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of grid points (used when `new_data` is `None`). [level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence level for intervals. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [CATEResult]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : ::: ### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the causal GAM via cross-fitted DML. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-cookbook/whittaker/causal.py#L337-L426){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit(data, *, fit_method="REML", select=False, seed=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Randomly assigns observations to `n_folds` folds, then for each fold fits an outcome GAM `E[Y | X]` and a treatment GAM `E[D | X]` on the remaining folds and predicts residuals on the held-out fold. The pooled cross-fitted residuals are combined into the partialling-out ATE estimate and its standard error (see class Notes). If `method="interactive"`, an additional CATE model is fit on the residual ratio. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [InputData]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Column-oriented data containing outcome, treatment, and confounder columns. [fit_method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["REML"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Smoothing parameter selection method for the outcome and treatment nuisance GAMs (default `"REML"`). [select]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Enable double-penalty variable selection in the nuisance GAMs. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for fold assignment. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [CausalGAM]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns `self` for method chaining. ::: ### [residuals()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return the orthogonalized residuals. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-cookbook/whittaker/causal.py#L575-L585){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python residuals() ``` ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[NDArray, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(residuals_y, residuals_d)`, a residualized outcome and treatment after partialling out confounders. ::: ### [summary()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Build a human-readable text summary of the fitted causal GAM. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-cookbook/whittaker/causal.py#L587-L623){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python summary() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Reports the outcome, treatment, confounders, estimation method, number of cross-fitting folds, and the treatment effect (ATE, standard error, confidence interval, and p-value) from `treatment_effect()`. If `method="interactive"` and a CATE model was successfully fit, notes that `.cate()` can be used for estimates. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Multi-line summary text. ::: ### [treatment_effect()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the average treatment effect with inference. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-cookbook/whittaker/causal.py#L454-L487){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python treatment_effect(level=0.95) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Builds a `TreatmentEffect` from the ATE and standard error computed during `fit()`, adding a normal-approximation confidence interval and two-sided Wald p-value for `H0: ATE = 0`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence level (default `0.95`). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TreatmentEffect]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : :::
